rv.q: With visual vibrance and refreshing honesty, Heartbreak Hotel pumps fresh blood into the breakup narrative.
The production style is holding back the genuinely interesting content of the show.
If the journey proves more taxing than transformative, it nonetheless leaves a distinct impression.

Ultimately, though, it is a brave attempt to examine seemingly every nook and cranny of love that goes wrong—it’s a strange breed of TED talk about breakup woes, illustrated with scenes of pain and discomfort, with the hope of recovery at the end.

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive New Zealand import for its creative exploration of romantic grief, with McCracken's vulnerable performance and the show's blend of music, monologue, and performance art earning positive notices.
